sections.overview: Troglodiplura lowryi is a cave-dwelling mygalomorph spider endemic to the Nullarbor Plain of southern Australia.
sections.identification: It is an unusually cave-adapted spider, but its original taxonomic study was hampered by fragmentary or juvenile museum material.
sections.habitat: Known records place it in caves on the Nullarbor Plain.
sections.diet: Reliable species-specific information about its prey was not available in the sources consulted.
sections.behavior: Its cave ecology remains poorly known, in part because adult specimens have been scarce in collections.
sections.reproduction: The sources consulted do not describe its courtship, egg-laying or development.
sections.ecology: It is one of the most strongly cave-adapted mygalomorph spiders known.
sections.conservation: An Australian government draft assessment proposed classifying it as data deficient for federal threatened-species listing; that was a consultation proposal, not a final status in the cited source.
